record.paper_title: A Survey on LoRa Networking: Research Problems, Current Solutions and Open Issues
record.original_question: How should LoRa networks dynamically choose each end-device’s communication parameters, including spreading factor, transmission power, bandwidth, channel allocation, data rate, and frame repetition rate, so that scalability, packet reception, energy consumption, and reliability improve across indoor, outdoor, high-noise, temperature-varying, and other deployment environments? A complete answer should account for environmental factors that existing dynamic-parameter methods omit, such as ambient temperature reducing signal strength, and should avoid assuming that simply increasing spreading factor always improves communication performance.

evidence.quote: In LoRa technology, the transmission is controlled by the parameters Spreading Factor (SF), Transmission power (TP), Bandwidth (BW) and Channel. Varying these parameters result in different transmission qualities. This can be leveraged to improve concurrent transmissions. Dynamically allocating reasonable resources to end-devices based on the deployed environment improves multiple access and thus scalability [85].
Finally, it is concluded that LoRa is highly robust to high noise levels and recommend further investigation by varying the ﬁxed parameters of this experiment.

Hakkenberg et al. [113] and Neumann et al. [114] evaluate the performance of LoRa in both indoor and outdoor environments and recommend that transmission parameters have to be varied according to the deployed environment.
Experimental result shows that a personalized communication parameter for each end-device will aid scalability.
Two suggested guidelines are to develop a protocol to decide communication parameters dynamically and to evaluate optimal gateway placement for better scalability.
It is shown that investing high energy for higher SF values does not always improve communication performance.
Network density can be scaled-up by adding more gateways and personalizing transmission parameters like data rate and channel allocation using ADR for each end-device [25], [66], [67], [69].
Hence, varying transmission parameters based on indoor/outdoor deployed environment gives better performance [113], [114].

Some solutions for choosing dynamic communication parameters consider most of the factors, but did not take into account the ambient temperature which plays a major role in reducing the signal strength [68].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a LoRa (Long Range) wireless network consisting of a set of end-devices E = {e_1, ..., e_N} communicating with one or more gateways. Each end-device e_i must, at every transmission instant t, choose a vector of communication parameters

  p_i(t) = (SF_i, TP_i, BW_i, CH_i, DR_i, FR_i),

where SF_i ∈ {7,8,9,10,11,12} is the spreading factor, TP_i ∈ [TP_min, TP_max] is the transmission power, BW_i ∈ {125, 250, 500} kHz is the bandwidth, CH_i is the channel index from a finite set of available channels, DR_i is the data rate, and FR_i ∈ ℕ is the frame repetition rate.

The deployment environment is described by an environmental state vector ε(t) which may include ambient temperature T(t), indoor/outdoor classification, ambient RF noise level, multipath/shadowing, and node mobility. The received signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio at the gateway and the corresponding packet reception probability depend on p_i(t), ε(t), and the joint choices {p_j(t)}_{j ≠ i} of other devices via standard LoRa link and capture models, with the additional realistic constraint that increasing T(t) decreases received signal strength, and that increasing SF does not monotonically improve link quality once interference and time-on-air are taken into account.

Define network-level objectives:
 (S) scalability: maximum number of end-devices supportable while keeping packet delivery ratio above a threshold;
 (P) packet reception ratio averaged over devices and time;
 (Q) average energy consumption per successfully delivered packet;
 (R) reliability, measured as the probability that each device achieves its target delivery ratio over a window.

Problem. Design a (possibly distributed) policy π: (history of local observations and feedback, ε(t)) → p_i(t), per end-device, such that for every environment trajectory ε(·) drawn from a class encompassing indoor, outdoor, high-noise, and temperature-varying conditions, the policy simultaneously improves S, P, Q, and R relative to any static or environment-agnostic parameter assignment, while

 (i) explicitly incorporating environmental covariates (in particular ambient temperature) into the parameter choice,
 (ii) not relying on the assumption that larger SF always yields better communication performance, and
 (iii) producing a personalized parameter vector p_i for each device rather than a network-wide uniform setting.

Characterize the existence, structure, and optimality guarantees of such a policy, and quantify the achievable trade-off region among (S, P, Q, R) as a function of the environmental class.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (ADR variants, reinforcement-learning-based parameter assignment, and environment-aware schemes published through 2024–2025) continues to propose partial solutions for subsets of the parameters (mainly SF and TP) and partial environmental factors, but no scheme jointly optimizes SF, TP, BW, channel, data rate, and frame repetition while incorporating environmental effects such as ambient temperature and avoiding the higher-SF-is-better assumption. The general problem remains open.

status_evidence.snippet: Dynamically allocating reasonable resources to end-devices based on the deployed environment improves multiple access and thus scalability.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open research problem in LoRa networking surveys.

status_evidence.title: Recent surveys on LoRa adaptive data rate and parameter selection
status_evidence.snippet: ADR and learning-based variants address SF/TP under limited environmental models; temperature effects and joint multi-parameter optimization remain unaddressed.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works provide only partial solutions.
